question.text:
Suppose we would like to find the maximum of the function $f(x,y,z)=xy^2z$ on the intersection of the surfaces $x^2-2z^2=1$ and $y^2+3z^3=5$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda$ and $\mu$ satisfy the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} \big\langle y^2z, \, \bbox[2pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}}, \, xy^2 \big\rangle = \lambda \big\langle 2x, \, 0, \, \bbox[2pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} \, \big\rangle + \mu \big\langle 0, \, 2y, \, \bbox[2pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AA}} \, \big\rangle \\[3pt] x^2-2z^2=1 \\[3pt] y^2+3z^3=5 \end{cases} \]

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?
question.explanation:
We need to find the maximum value of

\[ f(x,y,z) = xy^2z \]

subject to the constraints

\[ g(x,y,z)=x^2-2z^2=1, \qquad h(x,y,z)=y^2+3z^3=5. \]

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} \nabla f(x,y,z) = \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[3pt] g(x,y,z)=1 \\[3pt] h(x,y,z)=5 \end{cases} \]

We now expand the first equation of the system:

\begin{align} \nabla f(x,y,z) &= \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[5pt] \langle f_x, f_y, f_z \rangle & = \lambda \langle g_x, g_y, g_z \rangle + \mu \langle h_x, h_y, h_z \rangle \\[5pt] \langle y^2z, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2xyz}, \, xy^2 \rangle & = \lambda \langle 2x, \, 0, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}-4z} \rangle + \mu \langle 0, \, 2y, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}9z^2} \rangle \end{align}

We now expand the first equation of the system:

\begin{align} \nabla f(x,y,z) &= \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[5pt] \langle f_x, f_y, f_z \rangle & = \lambda \langle g_x, g_y, g_z \rangle + \mu \langle h_x, h_y, h_z \rangle \\[5pt] \langle 1, \, 2y, \, 1 \rangle & = \lambda \langle 0, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}6y}, \, 2z \rangle + \mu \langle 1, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0}, \, 2z \rangle \end{align}

Suppose we would like to find the minimum value of the function $f(x,y,z)=xy+z^2$ on the intersection of the surfaces $y-x=0$ and $x^2 + y^2 + z^2=4$ using the method of Lagrange multipliers. Then, the corresponding Lagrange multipliers $\lambda$ and $\mu$ satisfy the following system:

We need to find the minimum value of

\[ f(x,y,z) = xy+z^2 \]

subject to the constraints

\[ g(x,y,z)=y-x=0, \qquad h(x,y,z)=x^2 + y^2 + z^2=4. \]

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} \nabla f(x,y,z) = \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[3pt] g(x,y,z)=0 \\[3pt] h(x,y,z)=4 \end{cases} \]

\begin{align} \nabla f(x,y,z) &= \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[5pt] \langle f_x, f_y, f_z \rangle & = \lambda \langle g_x, g_y, g_z \rangle + \mu \langle h_x, h_y, h_z \rangle \\[5pt] \langle y, \, x, \, 2z \rangle & = \lambda \langle -1, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}1}, \, 0 \rangle + \mu \langle 2x, \, 2y, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2z} \rangle \end{align}

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the expressions?
question.explanation:
We need to find the maximum value of

\[ f(x,y,z) =3x+2z+y^2 \]

subject to the constraints

\[ g(x,y,z)=x^2+y^2=1, \qquad h(x,y,z)=2x^2+y^2+4z^2=1. \]

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

\[ \begin{cases} \nabla f(x,y,z) = \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[3pt] g(x,y,z)=1 \\[3pt] h(x,y,z)=1 \end{cases} \]

We now expand the first equation of the system:

\begin{align} \nabla f(x,y,z) &= \lambda \nabla g(x,y,z) + \mu \nabla h(x,y,z) \\[5pt] \langle f_x, f_y, f_z \rangle & = \lambda \langle g_x, g_y, g_z \rangle + \mu \langle h_x, h_y, h_z \rangle \\[5pt] \langle 3, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}2y}, \, 2 \rangle & = \lambda \langle 2x, \, 2y, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}0} \rangle + \mu \langle 4x, \, 2y, \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}8z} \rangle \end{align}
